sb_prompt: FIND OUT WHAT CRITERIA THE OTHER CALLER WOULD USE IN SELECTING CHILD CARE SERVICES FOR A PRESCHOOLER.  IS IT EASY OR DIFFICULT TO FIND SUCH CARE?
turns: Hey, so you got the call too? I was just about to hit that button. I'm an insurance adjuster by the way, and honestly, picking childcare for a preschooler is a nightmare if you look at it from a liability standpoint, though my own kid is actually in a place that works out fine. What about you? Are you doing this for your own family or just curious?
Yeah, actually for my own kid, and honestly it's brutal because as a store manager I see parents trying to juggle shifts with nothing available.

That's rough, I totally get the juggling act, especially with shifts. My daughter is in a spot where the owners have been there twenty years, but man, the waitlist is insane lately; we actually had to wait three months before they even called us back.
Three months?! That's crazy, but honestly, that's exactly why I'm so picky; I know a single mom next door who looked at five different spots before settling on a tiny family home down the street.
That's really admirable of her though, finding a family home usually means you have to vet the parents just as hard as the program itself.

It's crazy though, vetting a family is so much scarier than vetting a licensed center, I mean, if they slip up you're stuck with it, plus my neighbor mentioned she found out the dad was arrested last year and she had nowhere else to go.

Yeah, man, that's a whole other level of risk I never thought about; I'm pretty sure my kids' spot would have closed down if the owner had a record like that, and honestly, that's the part of this whole search that makes my head spin a little bit.
Yeah, honestly that's why I always go straight for the licensed centers if I can, even if the waitlist is long, because at least the paperwork proves they have some standards.
Right, but I guess that's why I'm stuck too, since my job means I can't just bail out if they screw up, so I'm praying that license is actually real and not just a piece of paper.

Yeah, exactly, and I guess that's the trade-off, you never get the safety net of an insurance claim if something goes wrong at a home, but at least the teachers there are trained to actually handle the kids right.
Yeah, trained teachers are a breath of fresh air if they don't end up playing games with your kid's schedule because the bus is late.
Yeah, and honestly the schedule thing is huge for me too, because when my kid gets sick I need to know the teacher can jump in without me losing my store hours.
Yeah, the schedule thing is terrifying too, because if the bus is late you basically lose your whole day and get fired for it.
Yeah, that's exactly why I'm terrified too because if the kid is sick and I'm stuck at the store, I could lose my whole shift and get in trouble with my boss.
I guess that's why I'm actually glad my kid is with someone who knows exactly when to pick them up, even if it means I have to sneak off early sometimes.
Yeah, I get that, and honestly I'm just lucky my mom can swap in at the last minute so I don't have to worry about my hours.
Yeah, that's the thing with my job, I'm constantly trying to figure out if I should trust someone's word or just demand receipts before I sign anything.
Yeah, I guess that's why I just try to keep a backup plan ready in case someone flakes on the promise.
Yeah, having a backup is the only way to stay sane, though I still feel weird just handing my kid off to a stranger no matter how much they promise.
Yeah, I totally feel that about the stranger thing, which is why I'd never do it with my own little one.
Yeah, that's exactly my fear too, handing them to a total stranger, though I guess I just have to trust my gut or something goes wrong and I'm on the hook for everything.
Yeah, I guess I just have to trust my mom's word since she's the only one I can rely on in a pinch.
Yeah, but at least you have her there, I just don't have that safety net when it comes to someone I don't know.
Yeah, that's exactly why I'm holding out hope that my mom's house has a proper license, even if she just runs it as a side thing.
Yeah, that's the whole thing, I just hope she actually pulled the paperwork together before the state came knocking.
Yeah, I guess that's the scary part because if she doesn't have the paperwork, I literally can't put my kid in there even if she's perfect.

Yeah, I guess that's the whole dilemma, because if the paperwork doesn't exist I'm legally on the hook if anything happens, but if I wait for the paperwork the waitlist eats up every single moment I have left to find a spot.
Yeah, that's the killer, there's no way to win, either you wait forever or you gamble on a stranger and hope you didn't just set your kid up for a lawsuit.
Yeah, so I guess I'm just stuck in the middle trying to figure out if the license is worth the wait or if I should just take the gamble.
Yeah, I think I'd take the gamble if it meant getting him into a good spot sooner rather than just watching him from the car window all day.
Yeah, I guess I'm just going to take the gamble if I can find a licensed spot sooner rather than sitting in the car like a lunatic.
Yeah, but honestly I'd rather wait a little longer if it means the teachers actually know how to handle a meltdown than just have them in a room with a stranger who has no idea what's going on.
Yeah, that's the thing, I don't want them just sitting there while I'm stressing out, even if it means waiting a little longer to make sure they're actually safe.
Yeah, because honestly nothing screams "trauma" like a kid screaming in a room with no one to calm them down.
Yeah, exactly, and if we can't get a spot soon, I'm just going to pray my gut is right about that one place even though the paperwork still hasn't arrived.
Yeah, that's exactly my fear too, if they mess up there's no one to call and I'm just stuck with the mess.
Yeah, I know that feeling all too well, but honestly, by the time the state inspects that place, I'm going to be sitting in the car window for who knows how long.
Yeah, if they don't pass the inspection you'd be in real trouble, but honestly I think I'll take the risk just so I don't have to watch him from the car forever.
Yeah, I think I might just bite the bullet and wait another month to make sure the inspection passes before I risk gambling with a stranger.
Yeah, but if they don't pass the inspection you're stuck with the kid in the car while you work, so I'll probably just trust my mom and hope for the best.
